segments.text: Good morning everyone.
This is November the 12th Georgia Public Service Commission committee meeting and thinking
out over the audience to be a good morning for me to sell popcorn I think before we get
started.
But we'll begin now with facility protection commissioner.
Thank you vice chair.
We will call to order the facilities protection committee and hear item C1 please.
Good morning commissioners item C1 consideration of commission approval of side consent agreements
and resolution of following Gufba violations that is A through M and I am Maritza Rivera
from the Gufba department.
Are there any questions or comments on item C1?
Hearing none we'll put that on the agenda.
There are no proposed regular agenda items so we can conclude the facilities protection
committee.
Thank you.
Now go to telecom commissioner Johnson.
Good morning everyone.
We will now open the proposed agenda for telecommunications item C1.
Good morning Tamika Starks item C1 is docket number 57419 consideration application from
Quanta telecommunication solutions for certificate of authority to operate telephone plant line
or system.
Everything is in order and staff recommends approval.
Any questions comments concerns with C1?
Hearing none we move it to the agenda item C2.
Item C2 is consideration of three proposed tariff revisions filed by TDS companies to
increase rates for residential voice bundles to its general exchange tariffs.
Everything is in order and staff recommends approval.
Any questions comments concerns regarding C2?
Hearing none we move it to the agenda.
We have one proposed regular agenda item.
Good morning commissioners.
My name is Erica Wilson.
I am a telecommunications analyst.
Our one is docket number 27825 consideration of the petition by Cobb County Board of Commissioners
to implement the abbreviated N11 Dowling Code 311 for non-emergency government services
in Cobb County, Georgia.
In its order dated September 18th, 2008, the Georgia Public Service Commission approved
assignment of the abbreviated Dowling Code 311 to Cobb County for use to provide access
to the county's non-emergency government services through its customer service center.
The order further provided that Cobb County shall be allowed six months to implement its
311 service.
On November 10th, 2008, Cobb County found a letter requesting a 12 month extension to implement
its 311 service.
Cobb County was unable to meet the March 18th, 2009 implementation deadline due to financial
setbacks in turn delaying the projected date for implementation of the 311 service.
On December 2nd, 2008, administrative session, the commission adopted staff's recommendation
to grant the extension.
On October 13th, 2009, Cobb County requested another extension noting financial hardships
due to flood damages to the call center and slow economic recovery.
Commissioned staff acknowledged the hardship and determined that an extension from the
commission was not required as 311 was already in service as required by the approval order.
Cobb County was informed to continue to notify in writing the commission staff of its progress
in placing the 311 Dowling Code into service.
On October 22nd, 2006, Cobb County found a letter noting full implementation of the 311
service by Cobb County government consistent with the September 18th, 2008 order, additionally
noting that back on July 28th, 2026, Cobb County government approved funding for staffing
the 311 call center and are now ready to implement the 311 service to citizens of Cobb
County, Georgia.
The anticipated launch date of the customer service call center is January 7th, 2027.
Staff recommends that commission approve Cobb County's request to implement the abbreviated
in one Dowling Code 311 for non-emergency government services in Cobb County, Georgia.
Excuse me, additionally, Cobb County shall notify in writing the commission staff upon
approval full implement, I'm sorry, upon full implementation of the 311 call center.
Any questions, comments or concerns about R1?
Hearing none, we move it to the agenda.
Chair Johnson, I'm sorry, I had one question on items too, if you don't mind, and I apologize
for going back a little bit, but I didn't realize this at first.
Our item C2 is really just the question of, is this going to, I realize that the reason
for this is under recovery of a target ROE, but is there going to be a burden on the remaining
customers from this increase, this rate increase?
No, there will not be.
Even though it's going up by two to $5 a bill?
Yes, it's going to be going up by $2.
It will not be a significant increase or burden to the customers.
But there is an increase, and that's really just to maintain that target.
It is correct.
All right, thank you.
All right, circling back to R1, any questions, comments, concerns regarding R1?
Hearing none, we move it to the regular agenda.
If there are no other items, we will close out the agenda.
Thank you, Commissioner Johnson, and then we'll go to Energy, Commissioner Schill.
All right, Commissioner Wise is out.
I'll hand to Energy, and we'll start with C1 on the consent agenda.
Good morning, C1, docket number 57451, Coaster EMC, Application for Financial Authority.
Coaster EMC is seeking to obtain a new loan in the amount of $61 million with USDA RUS
with a term of 35 years.
The purpose of the loan is for 2026 through 2029 four-year construction work plan, which
includes approximately $14 million of reimbursement for completed projects.
Coaster EMC is in Midway, Georgia, with over 21,000 members.
Staff recommends approval.
All right, thank you.
Any questions on C1?
All right, it's on C2.
Morning.
Good morning, Commissioner.
My name is Ruth.
C2 is consideration of request for transfer of retail electric service by the following
customers A and B. Supporting documents have been reviewed, and I and others staff recommends
approval.
Any questions?
Did hanging dog roll the paved road or is it a dirt road?
All right, any questions on C2, A and B?
All right, it's on C3.
Good morning, Commissioners.
My name is Irma Armino from the Gas Unit.
C3 is docket number 57260, 2027, 2029, regulated provider of natural gas.
Consideration of staff's recommendation to issue a request for proposal for the selection
of the regulated provider for the upcoming term.
In light of the current regulated provider term coming to an end on August 31, 2027,
staff is bringing before the Commission a request for a proposal to select a new regulated provider
for the 2027, 2029 term.
Pursuant to the timeline on the RFP, the deadline to submit bids to staff will be
January 20, 2027, by 4 p.m.
The Commission will be selecting a new regulated provider by no later than May 2027.
Staff recommends approval.
Any questions on C3?
Thank you, it's on.
All right, we will move on to the regular agenda, starting with item R1.
Morning, John.
Good morning.
John Caden with the ERE unit.
Item R1 is docket number 4822.
This is capacity and energy payments to co-generators under the Public Utility Regulatory Policy
Act of 1978, consideration of updated state jurisdictional qualifying facility transmission
generator interconnection procedures.
On November the 5th, Georgia Power filed a request for Commission approval to update
the SJQF-TGIP, which is the state jurisdictional QF transmission generator interconnection procedures.
The updates would convert the QF interconnection process from a largely individual request-driven
serial study framework into a formal annual cluster study process.
Southern Companies SJQF-TGISP, which is incorporated into Georgia Power's Commission approved
SJQF-TGIP, by reference, say that interconnection requests may be studied serially or in clusters.
Georgia Power, in its November 5th filing, stated that for ease of review and administration,
the revised procedures combine the interconnection procedures and study process document into
one document.
The revised procedures provides QF instructions on how to request interconnection and describes
how the company will study state jurisdictional QF interconnection requests going forward.
The QF cluster study process is fully described in the updated document, making it reference
to the Southern Companies study process document no longer necessary.
The revised procedures mirror many of the Southern Companies' FERC-approved annual cluster
study processes.
There are many aspects of the current process that will remain in place in the updated
procedures, such as the cost of the application deposit, the study deposit tiers, as well
as the true open refund provisions.
Staff has met with the company to discuss the company's proposed changes to the process
document to understand the impact to current procedures and assess the effect to future
QF projects.
Staff has reviewed the updated procedures and recommends approval of Georgia Power's request
to update the SJQF-TGIP, which would effectuate and change the state jurisdictional QF interconnection
study process from a serial to a cluster study.
Thank you.
Thank you, John.
Thank you.
Are there any questions on our one?
Yeah, a few questions, Mr. Kadick.
Do you know how many QF requests for interconnection come in a year?
I don't off-end, no.
That might be a question.
Eight to 15?
I've been told eight to 15 probably within the last year.
Okay, eight to 15.
And another question, in the request on page three, there was a quote that the revised
procedures would mirror many of the Southern Companies' FERC-approved annual cluster
process, but not all?
Yes.
Do you know what's different about the larger cluster study process?
Sure.
The FERC study process is just an interconnection study process, and the QF study process for
Georgia Power includes both interconnection and the delivery-related study process, so
that's where they diverge on their timeline.
And plus, FERC study process includes what they call it readiness deposits and other
cost responsibilities if generators back out of the process at some point, and the
Georgia Power interconnection process does not do these QF.
So it's a little bit more, less stringent than the FERC process.
I thought I saw that there is a deposit as you go into the interconnection process.
There is a deposit.
There's not millions of dollars like there is in the FERC process.
Okay.
You're right.
There's like $125,000 for a greater than 20 megawatt project, but other than that,
there are not the multi-million dollar.
Okay.
I do see the benefit of studying as a cluster, but there's also, I didn't see a
quantification of that, or there's certainly certainty and clarity for the developer on
that process, although if they miss that window, they have to wait a full year to
jump into the next process.
Do you know if staff or the company reached out to any of these QF existing customers,
prospective customers, to get their feedback on going from serial to cluster?
We have not.
Okay.
Does the company did?
That's not a question for that.
Okay.
Okay.
I guess those are all the questions I have.
Lenny.
All right.
Another quick question.
Sure.
Do we feel like we need to set some firm study deadlines and annual performance
reporting, and if so, what does staff recommend the report include and what those
intervals will be?
In the process document itself, on page 9 of 24, there is a timeline in here that's
out the engagement window, notice in window, scoping meetings, where the phase
one study report, approximate time for that, site visits, phase two study
report, and then final report.
And it says this starts in about April of each year, and we conclude somewhere
around, well, execution of QFAs in June of the following year.
Okay.
John, can you just refresh this?
I know several years ago, we had an influx of these HRPA projects coming in,
and some of them had extremely high interconnection costs associated, and we
had to make some changes to deal with that and to ensure that, in this case,
the developers are on the hook for all of those interconnection costs so they
couldn't be.
Since this is not part of our RFP process where you're able to have
evaluation methodology applied, so what we did back then is that, are you
confident that it's working to ensure that the interconnection costs are
being borne by the developers?
It is, and in those recent times, all the interconnection costs were borne
by the QF developer.
What was up for decision was the network upgrades, and that's where a lot
of those costs were coming in, but you're right, all those costs are still
on the developer except for anything that's in the 10-year transmission
plan, those upgrades would be refunded, but yes, it is working, and it's
all assigned to the developer otherwise.
Thank you.
All right, any other questions?
All right, R1 is on, and we'll move on to R2.
And staff would request this be moved to the consent agenda, if that's...
Any objection to moving R1 to the consent agenda?
All right, it's on the consent.
We'll move it to consent.
Thank you, John.
We'll move on to R2.
Good morning, commissioners.
Justin Pawlik, commission staff attorney.
Item R2 is consideration of what's been styled an emergency appeal from an order
issued by the hearing officer in docket number 57243, petition for
expedited declaratory judgment and enforcement against Voltergrid.
The motion was filed with the commission on Monday, November 9th,
2026, by Voltergrid LLC, a party in the docket and is an appeal of the
hearing officer's order issued last Wednesday, November 4th, 2026.
By way of background, docket 57243 concerns a petition filed with
the commission on July 13th.
The petitioners, Sustainable Newton, a Georgia nonprofit organization,
Sarah and Randall Vincent, Theodosia and William Wade, Georgia residents,
alleged generally that respondent Voltergrid is constructing a 90-megawatt
power plan in Covington, Georgia, with the intent to provide electrical service
to an adjacent data center to be owned and operated by a separate business
entity, commonly referred to as server farm.
The petitioners contend that the provision of such electrical service
violates Georgia territorial acts and server farms located in territory
previously signed by the commission of Georgia Power Company.
The petitioners also claimed the provision of electrical services as a
server farm would violate the Georgia Cogeneration Distribution Act of 2001.
For relief, the petitioners have requested the commission determine and
declare whether Voltergrid LLC is planning to construct and operate a
power plant to furnish retail electric service in violation of the
Territorial Act and order that Voltergrid LLC cease and desist any
operations in violation of the Territorial Act or Cogeneration Act.
On August 24th, 2026, the commission signed the petition to hearing
officer, Mr. Chris Collado, ordering that the hearing officer will issue a
procedural and scheduling order setting the matter down for hearing on issues
set forth in the petition and on whether the respondent is providing
service that is subject to the jurisdiction of the commission, and if
so, what if any action the commission should take.
The hearing officer then issued a notice and scheduling order setting the
matter down for hearing on December 9th.
On August 31st, staff issued Data Request STF PIA-1 in the docket,
which included questions for Voltergrid and requests for various categories of
documents, including copies of all agreements between server farm and
Voltergrid communications with the city of Covington relating to gas
service for the project and documents reflecting statements by Georgia
Power Company about the provision of electric service to server farm.
In response, Voltergrid produced around 4,700 pages of documents in
trade secret and public disclosure format.
Staff received unredacted trade secret format, and the petitioners and
interveners in the case, which includes Georgia EMC, received redacted public
disclosure versions.
About 1,000 pages were redacted in their entirety, and the remainder
include numerous partial redactions, although some of those redactions and
trade secret designations have since been removed, and I believe it's 45
documents that are still trade secret.
Voltergrid did provide the petitioners and interveners with a heavily
redacted version of the executed contracts between Voltergrid and server
farm.
The redacted information includes but is not limited to pricing schedules,
project timetables, and technical schematics for the project.
On September 16th, 2026, Voltergrid filed a motion to dismiss.
Motion is not clear in my opinion as to whether Voltergrid is seeking
merely to remove the petitioners from the proceedings or whether Voltergrid
is seeking full resolution of the issues identified by the hearing
officer in the notice of hearing and scheduling order.
In its brief and supportive motion to dismiss, Voltergrid challenges
whether the petitioners are interested parties under the Territorial
Act such that they have standing to petition the commission for relief
under the Territorial Act.
Voltergrid also argues at length that its provision of services to
server farm is not in violation of the Territorial Act, generally on
the grounds that it is not providing public utility service or otherwise
acting in the capacity of a public utility.
Counsel for Voltergrid has requested an expedited decision on the
motion to dismiss and has repeatedly asserted that a ruling on the
motion is required before there is a hearing on the merits or whether
any other matter should be considered.
The hearing officer has not scheduled a hearing on the motion or
otherwise indicated when he might rule on the motion.
On October 2nd, the petitioners filed a motion challenging Voltergrid's
trade secret designations and requesting access to unredacted documents
under a nondisclosure agreement pursuant to commission trade secret
rules.
There was extensive briefing by the parties that is filed in the
docket.
During the next several weeks, commission staff strongly encouraged
the parties to resolve their dispute on their own without with an
appropriate NDA or consent protective order.
However, the parties were not able to come to an agreement and
the hearing officer conducted a hearing on the petitioners motion on
October 29th.
At the hearing, staff took the position that the public benefit of
providing the petitioners and their counsel access to the information
outweighed the potential harm to Voltergrid of such disclosure.
Staff did not take a position on whether Voltergrid's trade secret
designations were justified or on any of the merits of the petition,
including whether the petitioners have standing or are otherwise proper
parties under the Territorial Act or the Co-Generation Act.
At the hearing, Voltergrid had the full opportunity to present
evidence both as to the potential harm it would suffer if the
information were to be disclosed and as to any public benefit to the
disclosure.
Voltergrid did in fact present witness testimony from its chief
legal officer as to the information contained in the documents.
Staff have also taken the position that the hearing officer
should reserve his decision on the issues and the motion to
dismiss until after the hearing on December 9th in the interests
of judicial economy because of staff's interpretation of the
commission's order signed in this case for a hearing by the
hearing officer on the issues raised in the petition necessarily
implies that the petitioners have a meaningful opportunity to
participate in the hearing.
On November 4th, as I said last Wednesday, the hearing officer
issued a written decision ordering that Voltergrid and the
petitioners enter into a nondisclosure agreement and file
that agreement with the commission by 4 p.m. today,
November 12th.
The hearing officer also ordered that pursuant to that NDA,
Voltergrid immediately provide the petitioners with access to
all redacted documents produced in response to staff that
request STFPIA 1.
As I previously stated, Voltergrid filed what has been
styled its emergency appeal of the order on Monday, November
9th.
The appeal is a lengthy one around 21 pages and I believe has
been provided under the backup for this item.
In general, Voltergrid argues that the hearing officer did
not have authority under the commission rules to grant the
petitioners access to the redacted information, that the
hearing officer did not follow proper procedure in holding a
hearing or in issuing the order, and again, that the
motion to dismiss should be decided before any other issue
in the case, including allowing the petitioners access to the
requested information.
By way of action from the commission, Voltergrid has
requested that the commission one, immediately stay the
order in its entirety, including the November 12th,
2026 deadline to file an executed protective agreement,
which is due today, and the directive that access be
granted upon execution pending the commission's decision on
this appeal.
Two, vacate the orders grant of access to Voltergrid's
protected information and its directive that Voltergrid
execute a protective agreement.
Three, hold that the trade secret motion in a
advance until Voltergrid's motion to dismiss is decided.
Four, if the trade secret motion is thereafter heard,
conduct a hearing and a document by document in camera
inspection of the 45 documents identified in Voltergrid's
notice before the commission under rule 515-3-1-0.11
subsections three and seven.
With any testimony or argument concerning the content of
protected information taken in closed session.
Five, confirm that any order determining that protected
information is not a trade secret or must be disclosed
automatically stayed for 30 days under the same rule
and may stay any such order pending judicial review.
And six, grant such other relief as just and proper.
Because there are numerous legal issues involved in this
case, as commission staff attorney, I'm available to answer
any questions from the commission as best I can.
Mr. Turkey and the electric unit staff have also done
some analysis of the Voltergrid project from an economic and
engineering perspective.
And Mr. Turkey is also here with me to answer any policy or
technical questions.
Thank you.
Well, this issue is a tremendous issue because we have in
our state, this idea of onsite generation growing and it
doesn't give us as regulators insight into what's really
happening in terms of regulation and economic regulation on
these islanded facilities.
So, you know, I have specific concern about this and power
supplied outside of our utility system that can escape this
commission's oversight also have concern and growing concern
about confidentiality being a recurring barrier to our
oversight states or state entities, agencies, and so on
should not be signing NDAs when we're using public funds.
So having non-disclosure agreements between large loads and
utilities need to not be commonplace in Georgia because it
limits what regulators and the public can see.
So as we consider this issue before us chairman, there's a lot
for us to think about.
Okay, I certainly agree with that.
I guess my first question though is to staff and I'm sure
there's others that want to speak on this, but did the
hearing officer review all of this redacted information prior
to making any, well, I know they haven't made the decision
on the true matter at hand of whether or not this is a
violation of the Territorial Act, but I want to make sure
that staff has had access to the information because I
would think that the contract itself, for instance, would
be of utmost importance.
That is correct Commissioner and staff have reviewed the
documents, again, as I said, in their unredacted form.
At the hearing, the chief legal officer testified about
the information that was contained in the documents.
The respondent Voltergrid has asserted in this case that
an in-camera review was required for the commissioner,
for the hearing officer before making this determination.
However, under the commission rules of subsection three,
as to whether access should be granted, there is no mention
of an in-camera review by the hearing officer.
So, staff's legal position on that is that an in-camera
review is not required to make that determination
as to whether access is granted.
Now under subsection seven of the rule, there is a statement
that after a hearing and in-camera review
by the hearing officer that there will be determination
as to whether trade secret status has been determined.
That issue is still out there.
The hearing officer deferred any decision on whether
the information merits trade secret protection
to the commission.
So, our position is that for the purposes of this order
by the hearing officer, there was no in-camera inspection
that was required.
But again, there was testimony as to the information
that was contained in the documents
from Voltergrid's witness and there was an opportunity
for cross-examination on those issues.
So, the short answer is yes,
staff has reviewed the documents.
And the contract is one of the key pieces of information
that staff would like to see provided
to the interveners in this case.
They do have, as I said, a redacted version
that has some redactions that would appear
at least to staff to be proper as to pricing tables
and construction schedules
and the technical schematics for the project.
But again, the commission's policy as we,
the staff have understood is always be liberal
in granting access to information to parties
and interveners in cases.
Whereas, trade secrets being a little bit
more stringent requirement.
What is your response to some of the challenges made
in the appeal around what they're saying
about the hearing officer exceeded his authority
and that the hearing officer's powers
are limited to conducting the hearing
and building the record and then basically
even their compelling that there's compelled disclosure
raises constitutional concerns that the commission
should address before any disclosure.
I mean, what is your response to these challenges?
As I said, commissioner, there are numerous issues
that are raised in the appeal.
As to the constitutional issue,
again, I've heard it described that way
that there's a property interest in trade secrets
under the constitution that that interest
is subject to due process rights.
That's why we have the rules that we have.
That's why we have the procedures that we have.
There was a hearing, testimony was presented.
I'm not aware of any case law that says that
any additional due process is required
before the commission or its officers
can order that disclosure.
It is staff's position that the hearing officer
does have the necessary authority as part of its authority
to regulate the course of the hearing
and develop that record,
that that necessarily includes the right
to at least provide access.
And I think the hearing officer was very judicious
in making that determination and then reserving
the issue of trade secret protection
for the commission itself.
Again, one of the big issues in this case
is whether or not the petitioners have standing
and the respondent has repeatedly asserted
that that needs to be decided first
and also whether the commission has jurisdiction.
We believe that the commission clearly has
subject matter jurisdiction under the case,
under the Territorial Act and the enforcement provisions
in the Territorial Act.
Whether or not there is standing
or any of these other preliminary issues,
again, those are issues that should be decided
after the December 9th hearing.
In accordance with the commission's prior order
that there be a hearing on December 9th on those issues.
Can we allow targeted review of those most sensitive terms?
Again, that's for the parties decide commissioner
and this is something that staff has encouraged
that the parties have communications
to be able to work out something more specific
to the particular information that they're looking.
But it's difficult when you can't see the information
to make the determination.
So since there was no agreement,
the hearing officer was really sort of forced
to make a decision on the issue.
And again, the standard in this case
is whether or not the public interest
outweighs the potential harm
to the party whose information is being disclosed.
The petitioners in this case
are not competitors of Volta Grid
and there was testimony on this issue at the hearing
that they are not affiliated in any way with any competitors.
Also, their counsel attorneys,
Sherry or Whitfield and Kamani have appeared
before the commission on numerous occasions
and have received sensitive information in the past
and have took prudent measures
to not disclose that information.
We believe that there is very minimal risk
to harm to Volta Grid for this disclosure
and that that outweighs the potential risk to Volta Grid
that the information be disclosed.
Yeah, I think that terms bearing on ownership, control,
the sale and delivery of electricity in our state
and any duration should be produced for review.
No, I'm sure Mr. Galloway
would like to be heard on this as well.
I'm sure.
I've got one more question.
In terms of the timing on this,
it's a little confusing.
Normally when we have a committee agenda item
to be discussed and it's either held
or moved to the agenda for a vote following admin next week,
but we've got a deadline on this appeal.
How has that affected?
Can you explain that?
I mean, are we gonna need to make a decision
prior to the deadline or can we punt the deadline out
until we've had a chance to further review all this
and have a vote on it next week?
That's a really good question, Mr. Chairman,
especially since this appeal was only filed on Monday.
It's 21 pages long.
The respondents have not fully had an opportunity.
I'm sorry, the petitioners have not had a full opportunity
to respond with a brief.
And although I'm sure they would like to be heard as well.
Well, we're gonna get to that.
And I'm sorry for y'all that have taken the time
to be here as public witnesses today,
because that's for the next hearing to follow,
but this is our committee process
and it is a little bit lengthier than normal today
because we do have some important agenda items
and go ahead, Commissioner.
Mr. Chairman, as we've heard,
there are many, many issues that are to be decided
or to be discussed.
There's only one issue that I have
and I've been there from day one.
Does this violate the territorial rights act?
And I will stick with that until it has been proven to me
that this project does not violate the territorial rights act.
All the rest of it will be null and void
if it violates the territorial rights act.
Well, Commissioner, it is staff's interpretation of the order
that there be hearing on that on December 9th.
And that's what we hope will be decided
by the hearing officer
after there's been a full opportunity for the parties
to have their case heard.
All the rest of it's fine and well and good
if we want to take time to talk about it,
but we've got to decide that one issue
before anything else is meaningful.
Brief comment and question.
I agree with the significant jurisdictional issues raised
on whether or not the authority there,
the commission has the authority to address this.
But I also wanted to ask,
and I do take exception to the idea
that the commission lacks the authority
to provide the withheld documents
under a protective agreement.
So I just wanted to ask,
you mentioned that the petitioners had previously engaged
in consent protective agreements.
I mean, is this an unprecedented thing
to have a consent protective agreement
to allow this kind of information?
Has there ever been an incident
where information was released inadvertently
or that consent protective agreement was violated?
Trying to understand if this is an unprecedented move
to provide this kind of information to a petitioner.
Again, commissioner, it's my understanding
that the commission has always taken sort of a liberal policy
on allowing access to information with a few exceptions.
I'm not aware of any instances
where sensitive information has been disclosed
by an intervener or a petitioner case.
Again, they are represented by competent counsel
who appreciate the importance of trade secret protection
and following the rules
and the procedure set forth by the commission.
Thank you.
All right.
All right, I'm gonna let staff step back
and I'll invite any interested parties
that would like to address us.
There's a lot of paperwork.
It always is.
Good morning, commissioner Newton Galloway
on behalf of Vulture Grid.
Y'all caught me by surprise being on the dais this morning.
So I'm gonna ask Ms. Lindel to come up
because I wanted to convey some documents
in order to speed this along
so she can convey it to you.
And commissioner Johnson, I didn't realize
whether you would be here or not.
We will provide whatever is provided to you as well
after the meeting.
We are here in this case on an appeal
from the hearing officer's decision
that required the production of all documents
designated by Vulture Grid for trade secret protection
to the other parties.
They have not yet reached the issue
and have not addressed the two preliminary matters
that we think do have to be addressed,
which is that sustainable Newton,
the Wade's and the Vincent's do not have standing
to initiate a complaint under the Territorial Act.
And that is significant
because this is the first time of which I'm aware
that individuals have come in under the Territorial Act
to make that complaint.
And the issues they have have nothing to do
with the deficiencies of electrical service
